transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-25 16:30 UTC | Duration 52m
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jonah Park (CSM) — Dana Ortiz (Marigold Head Procurement), Marcus Lee (Marigold CISO), Priya Shah (Marigold Legal), Owen Greene (Marigold Platform)

Summary (auto): intake call to map legal and procurement checkpoints, identify PHI constraints, and price the Dedicated/Hosted options.

00:00 Dana Ortiz: okay uh thanks everyone for joining, I think we have the main folks here from our side. we wanted to walk through the approval lanes and what you need from us to unblock procurement, right Dana?
00:14 Alex Kim: yeah thanks Dana, appreciate it. i'll give the short overview from our side, then priya will go thru a technical preflight, and jonah will note timelines. the two main asks i heard were: PHI handling and key management, and to see a clear pricing lane for dedicated capacity, correct?
00:33 Marcus Lee: yeah that's right, plus encryption at rest and egress controls. our security team needs KMS boundary details and an option for customer-managed keys.
00:45 Priya Nair: just to clarify, we support BYOK via KMS integrations and HSM-backed key wrapping; in the Private / VPC package there's an option to bring your own key and we can show egress restrictions - there's also a Redwood Privet (sic) mode people call privet but it's the Private control plane.
01:05 Priya Shah: legal - i just want to understand the MSA redline process. our counsel will want DPA language that covers PHI, retention, and breach notification windows. what's your typical SLA for latency and availability?
01:20 Alex Kim: typical hosted SLA is 99.5% with latency SLOs published per model; Dedicated pools can be contractually backed with higher uptime and fixed throughput. for PHI we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated depending on throughput needs.
01:38 Marcus Lee: can you put the throughput numbers in the pricing matrix? we care about p95 < 300ms for chat flows; if it's >500ms it won't work for some clinical paths.
01:55 Priya Nair: noted. for sequence lengths we usually see p95 latency bump; if you pin a shorter max seq and use prefix caching we can keep p95 in the 200-350ms range on p4/8 configs, but yes depends on model and quantization profiles.
02:18 Owen Greene: quick question about caching: does the KV cache persist across restarts in Dedicated? we've had mis-synced caches on other vendor runs.
02:30 Priya Nair: good question, in our Dedicated offering cache is persisted within the runtime node and we have mechanisms to warm it during rolling updates; we call it continuous batching + KV cache but some transcripts show 'K V cash' which is funny.
02:50 Dana Ortiz: (laughs) noted. ok procurement-wise we have two lanes: one for standard SaaS onboarding (fast lane 2–3 weeks) and an escalated security lane (4–8 weeks) if there are DPA exceptions. we need to know which lane you expect us to follow.
03:10 Alex Kim: we typically start with fast lane for hosted with SOC2+ISO attestation. if you need PHI and customer keying we'll likely go escalated lane because of DPA exceptions and KMS verification, so plan 4–6 weeks.
03:28 Priya Shah: do you have a DPA template that includes the business associate agreement language for PHI?
03:35 Alex Kim: we have a DPA + BAA addendum we can share; i'll include it with the MSA redline.
03:40 Marcus Lee: also want to discuss billing egress fees - on previous providers we've been surprised by cross-region data transfer charges. how do you meter egress?
03:52 Alex Kim: billing model: tokens + optional dedicated capacity fee + bandwidth/egress separate line item. egress is metered per GB and depends on region pairs; we'll include an egress estimate based on your traffic profile if you share sample volumes.
04:10 Dana Ortiz: i'll need the pricing matrix to show procurement leadership. our approval threshold is $150k annual without exec signoff. above that we need a formal committee review.
04:22 Jonah Park: we'll provide a tiered pricing matrix and example commit options; also an expected pilot cost to fit under your threshold for initial evaluation.
04:35 Priya Nair: technical preflight notes — network: we need to confirm outbound allowlist IPs or private VPC peering; for Private we can operate entirely in your VPC and avoid egress across public net but there is more setup time.
04:58 Owen Greene: peering is preferable, we can do VPC peering but need a preflight diagram. i'll share our network diagram after the call.
05:10 Priya Shah: about indemnity and liability caps, will MSA have standard limits? our legal team tends to push for higher caps for PHI incidents.
05:22 Alex Kim: standard MSA has standard liability caps but we can discuss exceptions; typically those escalate to senior negotiators and might affect pricing/escrow options.
05:35 Marcus Lee: do you support SSO and SCIM for role-based access? we need RBAC and audit logs for token usage.
05:45 Alex Kim: yes SSO/SAML + SCIM are supported; audit logs are available in Redwood Console and we can export token-level traces needed for compliance.
05:58 Dana Ortiz: great. procurement question: can you provide a single contact for SOC2 evidence and pen test reports? our vendor team expects a package.
06:08 Alex Kim: yes we'll share the security pack and SOC2 report; i'm adding that as an attachment link post-call.
06:20 Priya Nair: circling back to pilot — scope recommended: 1) Hosted baseline for 2 weeks to validate latency and accuracy on non-PHI data, 2) Dedicated small pool for PHI workloads in Private mode as a combined next step if baseline passes.
06:38 Marcus Lee: that sequencing seems reasonable. timeline wise we need pilot results before Feb 28 to make a decision in March.
06:48 Jonah Park: noted. we'll aim to propose pilot week starting 2026-02-09 if we get approvals.
07:00 Priya Shah: legal will need to redline the MSA quickly; please send editable doc, not just PDF.
07:08 Alex Kim: yes editable. i'll send a track-changes doc and a clean PDF for procurement.
07:15 Dana Ortiz: one more on pricing — do you offer a committed spend discount if we commit to 12 months Dedicated?
07:24 Alex Kim: yes, committed capacity discounts available; i'll include a few commit tiers (monthly, 6-month, 12-month) and the unit rate delta.
07:35 Marcus Lee: competitor question — our team evaluated LargeCloudAI and OptiServe; both had either higher latencies or onerous keying flows. can you summarize where Redwood sits?
07:47 Alex Kim: short answer: we aim for production predictable latency with tooling to tune batching/caching and clear BYOK integration; i'll include a short competitive note in the packet.
07:58 Priya Nair: technical caveat — quantization profiles can reduce memory and cost but may have quality tradeoffs; we'll recommend model+quant combo in Optimize suggestions.
08:12 Owen Greene: what's the rollback policy if a Dedicated rollout causes regressions? we need safe fallback.
08:21 Priya Nair: rollouts support canary and automatic fallback to previous model variant—platform-level routing can route by latency or cost. we'll show the rollout UI in the deep dive.
08:35 Dana Ortiz: OK, to recap next steps?
08:40 Alex Kim: recap: i'll send MSA redline + DPA/BAA addendum + security pack; priya schedules technical deep dive (network + KV cache + KMS); jonah will propose pilot start week and pricing matrix; marigold to send data retention note and network egress diagram.
08:56 Priya Shah: thanks, we'll prioritize legal redlines and try to return comments within 72 hours.
09:02 Dana Ortiz: great thank you everyone, we'll look out for the docs and schedule.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors observed (e.g., "Redwood Privet" for Private, "K V cash" for KV cache). Some speaker labels overlap due to call recording quality.

End of transcript.
